name: warm_day_ceiling_breach_ac_defense__hvac_fan
description: [hvac_fan twin of golden 'warm_day_ceiling_breach_ac_defense'; Issue #1193] Core Issue #136 scenario. Warm day starts with outdoor below indoor (nat vent window). By mid-morning outdoor crosses above indoor and nat vent exits. User closes the window at 10:05 AM. ODE predicts indoor will reach comfort_cool=74F by 2 PM. The ceiling guard fires AC when predicted breach is within lead time and no window is open.
source: Issue #1193: hvac_fan twin of golden 'warm_day_ceiling_breach_ac_defense' (pre-#1140 version, fan configured). The golden is locked and now asserts the no-fan 'paused' result.
notes: This is the primary Issue #136 failure case: warm day where nat vent window closes due to outdoor warming,
ODE predicts a ceiling breach, but without the ceiling guard no AC would fire.
Modified for Issue #337: sensor_close at 10:05 AM models the user closing the window after nat-vent exits.
With Fix #337, _paused_by_door=True blocks apply_classification() when the window is open — so the ceiling
guard can only fire once the window is closed (_paused_by_door=False). This is the intended behavior:
CA does not force AC through an open window. The occupant must close the window (or use manual override)
to get cooling. The classification_suppressed_paused event covers the window-still-open case (see TestApplyClassificationPausedGuard).
The ceiling guard assertion (simulator_support=false) documents the expected behavior of the guard in automation.py.
The simulator CAN verify: nat vent activation at 8 AM, nat vent exit when outdoor crosses above indoor at 10 AM,
The simulator CANNOT verify: ODE ceiling guard firing because it requires _last_predicted_indoor curve and
k_passive/k_active_cool thermal model parameters which are runtime state, not simulated here.

hvac_fan twin (Issue #1193): with the HVAC fan configured, an open window with usable outdoor air is ventilation (fan on), not a pause. This scenario pins the ventilation/exit/setback decision only; it deliberately does NOT assert the cool setpoint that production also arms during hvac_fan ventilation (nat_vent_ac_assist_armed), which is the rule-3 question tracked in #1142.

events.note: Early morning: outdoor 62F well below indoor 72F. Nat vent conditions favorable.

Warm-day classification (forecast high 80 / low 60, matching the 62-76F readings): the classifier derives hvac_mode=off and windows_recommended=true for 06:00-10:00, so the 8:05 AM window opening is a planned window with a fan configured and starts nat-vent from the door/window handler itself (A3: the handler runs the nat-vent gate, no coordinator refresh involved). Indoor=72F >= comfort_heat=70F so no comfort-floor guard fires.
8 AM: outdoor 65F still below indoor 72.5F. Nat vent eligible.
User opens window. outdoor=65F < indoor=72.5F, indoor > comfort_heat=70F, outdoor <= threshold 77F — nat vent activates. _paused_by_door=False while nat-vent is active.
10 AM: outdoor has risen above indoor (73.5F > 73.0F). Nat vent exit fires — airflow would now add heat. _paused_by_door=True set by nat-vent exit.

User closes window after nat-vent exits (outdoor now warmer than indoor). _paused_by_door=False. Without this close, Fix #337 would block the ceiling guard — CA does not force AC through open windows.

12:30 PM: window is closed, _paused_by_door=False. ODE predicts indoor will reach 74F by 2 PM. Ceiling guard evaluates on this 30-min cycle. k_active_cool not learned — 120-min fallback applies. Breach is 1.5h away, within 120-min lead time.
2:30 PM: AC has run and indoor dropped back to 73F. ODE no longer predicts a breach. Guard goes dormant.

assertions.reason: [hvac_fan twin] Warm-day classification applied: hvac_mode=off. Indoor=72F >= comfort_heat=70F so HVAC off immediately without comfort-floor guard.
[hvac_fan twin] sensor_open: outdoor=65F < indoor=72.5F, indoor=72.5F > comfort_heat=70F, outdoor=65F <= threshold 77F — nat vent activates.
[hvac_fan twin] temp_update: outdoor=73.5F >= indoor=73.0F — directional exit fires at 10:00; airflow would now add heat rather than cool.

Issue #1230 R6 (owner-approved edit): the thermostat has been on cool since the 10:05 window close, so NO mode write is sent in the half hour -- the guard does not re-send 'cool' (before: one set_hvac_mode cool at 12:30). The band re-sends only the unchanged 74 F setpoint.

Issue #1230 R6 (owner-approved edit): at 12:30 the comfort band has already put the thermostat on cool at 74 F (indoor 73.8 is inside the cool arming margin), so the thermostat is cooling at the ceiling before the guard runs. The occupant's guarantee is the thermostat state, not a 'guard fired' label: it is told cool at 74 F.

Issue #1230 R6 (owner-approved edit): the guard sees a breach predicted within the lead time but the thermostat already cools at or below its 74 F ceiling, so it sends nothing and records no 'ceiling_guard_fired' row (before: a redundant cool + set_temperature 74 pair and an Activity row 'setpoint 74 -> 74'). It still fires when the thermostat is off, in heat, or cooling above the ceiling.

assertions.note: After the ceiling guard fires AC and indoor drops to 73F, ODE no longer predicts a breach. On the next 30-min cycle, _find_ceiling_breach_time() returns None. Guard evaluates and does nothing — HVAC stays at current state.
assertions.reason: [hvac_fan twin] Post-AC-run: ODE breach no longer predicted; ceiling guard goes dormant on next cycle. In production: HVAC reverts to warm-day classification (off) once indoor is below comfort_cool.

verdict.summary: [hvac_fan twin] Warm day with outdoor crossing above indoor: nat vent exits, user closes window, ODE ceiling guard fires AC defense before indoor reaches comfort_cool
verdict.observed_behavior: Confirmed failure 2026-05-11: HVAC stayed off, 3-hour comfort gap when indoor reached 75F
verdict.expected_behavior: Ceiling guard fires at noon cycle when breach predicted within 120-min fallback lead time and window is closed; AC defends comfort ceiling
